name: Unibot router unvalidated external call
summary: The direct Unibot router's externally callable function 0xb2bd16ab accepted an unvalidated external target and calldata without binding the token owner to the caller or an authorized Unibot operator. It therefore made attacker-selected transferFrom calls as the approved router, allowing the original exploiter to pull tokens from wallets that had approved it.
notes: Transaction 0xca799f...5724b directly created router 0x126c9f...1865. Its code is absent at block 18450357 and its 23,718-byte runtime has hash 0x16524e...5521c at both block 18450358 and the pre-anchor block 18467789. The anchor trace calls that address directly 17 times and shows no DELEGATECALL from it, while the EIP-1967 implementation and beacon slots are zero.

This record covers only the original 0x413e4f... exploiter's Ethereum campaign; later copycats are not added. Its 22 successful drain transactions run from the anchor through 0x3efea1... at block 18468232:28. Receipt and call-trace enumeration finds 299 successful victim-to-attacker transferFrom calls and matching Transfer logs, spanning 254 unique victim addresses and 22 token contracts. The often-reported 364-victim/42-token counts therefore appear to include attempted entries or broader activity and are not used as exact loss components. The attacker sold the stolen tokens through block 18468489 and then made 18 Tornado Cash deposits totaling exactly 355.5 ETH: three 100 ETH, five 10 ETH, five 1 ETH, and five 0.1 ETH deposits. CertiK independently reports 355.5 ETH of realized proceeds. This conservative realized-extraction measure avoids inventing incident prices for 22 mostly illiquid source tokens; swaps, copycat proceeds, and the team's later victim reimbursements are not added or netted against gross loss. DefiLlama's ETH observation 28 seconds before the anchor is 1800.0036569996832 USD, giving 639901.3000633874 USD and explaining the seed row's rounded 640000 USD figure.
